Hi guys. I am not Jewish, but very interested in Jewish philosophy and theology. I wanted to know if you would be interested in conducting an informal Talmud study. You would have to initiate me into the methods of study that are traditional, since naturally I am not familiar with them. It is exceedingly difficult to find courses online that are not chabad.org. (I have nothing against that site, but they do seem to have an agenda, and their resources are not exactly first rate). I cannot read Hebrew, which is problematic, but I can probably still get along. It would be helpful to dig into the material with those who have some exegetical experience with its terse, discursive mode of presentation. However, in all honesty, I am really just seeking a community that would be interested in drawing insights from this sprawling text--be it in a systematic, or, if need be, a more ad hoc manner.

Can't say that I am any authority on the Talmud, but if you're able to PM me and share your general whereabouts, I might be able to put you in touch with an in-person study group. Those seem much more numerous than e-study groups.

First, learn to read the Hebrew alphabet. The Talmud is written in Hebrew and knowing the basics the alphabet will help you immensely.

Next you buy this Aramaic-Hebrew dictionary. Every word I didn't knew I wrote it's meaning next to it. With enough words you can make out sentences. Once you finish a whole subject you should mind reading the narrative you find in translations or chabad to see if you somehow understood the subject of discussion.

In the beginning you start very slowly. Half a page in 2-3 hours but as you learn more you learn to distinguish where a sentence starts/ends, definition of words. If you want you can read Rashi commentary on the inside of the book (the side where the middle holds the book together), although for rashi you need to start learn Rashi Alphabet.

Anyway good luck.
